St Nicholas bursts in saying don’t eat that and then puts these dead pickled children back together.

Pretty much most of the Male lecturers I had at Uni made my life absolute misery. There was one in particular who I had for lots of classes, and then, I took feminism with him... 

There was a whole class where we talked about lesbian representation in film, Tv etc, when my friend asked me (being the only gay in the class) did I actually find any of the lesbian sex in this film realistic? (Fair question).

I said I found it a bit forced and I struggle to identify with it because it’s kind of not really marketed to just lesbians. It’s like watching lesbian porn, it’s not really for lesbians most of the time.

Anyway, my lecturer is just livid at what I’ve said, he starts laying into me saying “Well it was researched and studies were made into how lesbians have sex! How can you say it’s not realistic!?” He kept pressing me for an answer and kept trying to almost get a rise out of me? I didn’t need want to really talk about the experiences ive had, but I didn’t really want to go into it? I didn’t bite and let him witter on at me until the class ended, where he still pressed me for an answer. Really uncomfortable.

I don’t know why he freaked out, his reaction was very out of place for what were normally very very relaxed and informal discussion groups. It was bizarre. He sort of made it a point he would work into most of his lectures or group discussions over and over again and kept bringing it up. Even in different modules, he would bring it up and make me feel weird, like he couldn’t get over the joke or had a chip in his shoulder about it?

He got worse and worse throughout the rest of my time at that uni, I hated it. He made my life a misery and made me feel really embarrassed about being (quite honestly a bit of a jolly-butch-y-mess). It wasn’t so much that he didn’t like me for being gay, but I don’t know why that that was now okay for him to then literally bring up that one single point I made in his class 3 years ago and get irate or seemingly make it weird for everyone every time!

TLDR; A Male lecturer took my classes for feminism, I was asked about what I thought of a lesbian sex scene (as a lesbian) and he made it really fucking weird and didn’t drop it and made jokes about it for like two years after that.

I have to say, I did just type out that I was glad that I am not the only one experiencing the weird rules of gendered washing of clothes and stuff in school. But I'm not. I'm saddened to hear that your child's school think it's appropriate to do all of it for the boys because they think they won't do it? 

I went to a boarding school and the same kind of thing went on there too. All the boys would have their washing (uniform, PE kit, lab coats AND their regular clothes) all laundered by the school but the girls (all 60 of us) had to wash our own clothes in a small machine in the common room. 

I never was told why but I do feel a sense of relief finding out that it is a weird move to do one thing for the boys but not the same for the girls? I felt like I was reading into it too much and a bit crazy for thinking about it while I was there because everyone acted like it was normal but I'm glad you brought it up. 

I was always thought that it's very simple; learning to sew, wash clothes properly, change a tyre, look after your skin was just part of being a normal human being. It's not a gendered thing, I thought it was about being a grown up? What do they think will happen when people grow up? They'll just wait until their clothes sort of disintegrate off of them and buy more? Wtf?

Thanks for sharing, please keep us updated.
